cases.title: Test what the audience learns beyond the spoken process
cases.trigger: Narration lists professional work and explains compensation; an animation repeats successive actors/tasks.
cases.historical_decision: Move from a bounded broker dossier/work/fee study to one persistent business situated in the wider market, then expose the unpaid readiness role through compensation structure.
cases.evidence_vs_intent: R26 BRIEF explicitly aimed to reveal who carries risk and retained work in both fee outcomes. The owner still found it insufficiently additive. Do not rewrite this history as if R26 had no causal intent; a declared purpose did not establish comprehension or engagement.
cases.conditional_rule: Before choosing animation, state the new inference it enables and the exact visual relationship that makes it available. Prefer causal state, comparison, dependency or incentive logic over listing narrated steps. If nothing useful is added, hold the person, show evidence or simplify.
exceptions: A literal process diagram is useful when unfamiliar order, ownership or handoffs are the comprehension problem.
A funnel is appropriate only for supported convergence, filtering or attrition; it is not the default shape for business or broker content.
cases.review_question: Without hearing the list of tasks, can the viewer see who works, under what condition they are paid, and which job that structure leaves unassigned?
cases.outcome: Stronger R27 direction accepted with refinements; final R29 private prefix accepted.

cases.title: Widen the same business into a market only when comparison changes meaning
cases.trigger: Script shifts from the individual seller and broker to other sellers and selective buyers.
cases.historical_decision: Keep her workshop as the anchor, reveal surrounding businesses, then buyer comparison; return to the same workshop for the readiness question.
cases.evidence_vs_intent: Cue sheet distinguishes illustrative seller/buyer plurality from measured counts, conversion outcomes or a documented rejection. Runtime uses persistent business geometry and camera changes. No invented sale result is established.
cases.conditional_rule: Use a wider view when scale, competition or alternatives alter the audience's interpretation of the already established subject. Preserve an identifiable anchor and return to it when the argument becomes specific again.
exceptions: Do not fabricate measured crowd sizes or claim more choice from a source that does not establish it.
Do not pan/zoom simply to change the screen or force every business into an architectural metaphor.
cases.review_question: Can the viewer identify the original business before, during and after the widened market, and explain what the new alternatives change?

cases.title: A film-to-model seam must preserve the intended spatial relationship
cases.trigger: Owner wants the people in film to appear located inside the illustrated business.
cases.historical_decision: Remove the retained screenshot/inset and make the entire workshop drawn; R28 adds matching seller-left/buyer-right/table contours under one camera transform while film fades.
cases.evidence_vs_intent: R27 already removed retained photo but faded it over0.2s near the pullback start. R28 used matching people/table drawn contours plus a0.8s film fade during one2.75s world pullback. The rejected pre-correction inset is recorded by user feedback; no matching retained runtime is claimed.
cases.conditional_rule: When a designed transition says these people occupy this larger system, preserve actor positions, line of action, shared objects and camera origin across representations. Review midpoint as well as endpoints; fully complete the representation change.
exceptions: A photo inset can be appropriate as an attributed evidence window or deliberate mixed-media design, but that was not the intended relationship here.
A matched transition is unnecessary when a straight cut conveys the change more clearly.
Removing this optional model header does not authorize removing necessary source attribution, caveats or synthetic disclosure.
cases.label_decision: Owner removed ILLUSTRATIVE SUCCESS-FEE MODEL from picture; conceptual/synthetic provenance stayed in records and accessibility descriptions.
cases.review_question: During the pullback does the film become this drawn business, or look like a photograph placed on top of an unrelated diagram?
cases.outcome: R28 spatial bridge retained through R29 acceptance.

cases.title: Cut to a person when the argument changes to their stake or judgment
cases.trigger: A long system explanation shifts to seller reluctance, then to the host's central question.
cases.historical_decision: Insert seller film during no-cash/upfront-cheque reluctance and presenter during Here is the question through make it closeable. Return to animation for the answer and economic mechanism.
cases.evidence_vs_intent: The user requested meaningful interruptions and named the presenter phrase. R28 authoring chose the seller's financial reluctance for film; the resulting severe reaction was rejected. Changing medium did not by itself make the emotional choice right.
cases.conditional_rule: Give each cut one editorial job: human stake, question, consequence, evidence, orientation or reading relief. Tie entry and exit to the completed thought and source behavior. Retain system state while offscreen.
exceptions: Do not insert a cut on a fixed periodic cadence.
Do not cut away from a necessary visual operation before its consequence can be read.
A long hold is valid when it allows an unresolved human answer or diagram consequence to land.
cases.review_question: What does returning to this person add at this exact line, and what system state should the audience still remember afterward?
cases.outcome: Medium-role split retained; seller performance changed in R29.

cases.title: Let the host ask the question; reveal the answer when narration reaches it
cases.trigger: The script explicitly asks who is paid for readiness, then answers Nobody is.
cases.historical_decision: Exact question pickup begins review131.000/master134.000; closer crop before then who atreview139.958333; moving video ends143.041667; final source frame holds0.75s; gap begins143.791667, the first24fps frame after Nobody begins143.780.
cases.evidence_vs_intent: No exact-word existing presenter take was available; one authorized lips-only take was integrated. R28 recorded technical zero-lag and sampled/live checks while explicitly leaving performance approval open. Later owner acceptance applies to the exact private prefix. Seller film is narrated_dramatization; presenter delivery is bound to exact audible words.
cases.conditional_rule: Set rhetorical reveal limits before animating: what can be visible during the question and what must wait for the answer. Bind a speaking presenter to the actual narration range, with frame/sample-accurate boundaries and explicit hold strategy.
exceptions: Do not reuse unrelated visible speech as if it delivers these words.
Do not infer paid-generation permission from approval of a rough visual direction.
Do not prescribe0.75s holds or these crop scales to future episodes; fit natural pause and expression.
cases.review_question: Does the viewer get time to consider the question without seeing the answer early, and does the speaker visibly finish the exact phrase?
cases.outcome: Exact pickup and answer cut retained in R29 acceptance. Paid authorization was one attempt with no retries, not evergreen.

cases.title: Make absence specific, then show the mechanism producing it
cases.trigger: Narration says a hole has a specific shape, produced by how the people around it earn a living.
cases.historical_decision: Dedicated gap composition makes readiness work/no paid role a separate position between intact business and sale work. Trace its border on specific shape, then draw the conditional closing-fee path back to sale professionals while readiness stays unconnected.
cases.evidence_vs_intent: R27 contained a fee emphasis event that set paid-team opacity to1 when it was already1. R28 replaced that ineffective gesture with an actual fee-return edge; independent source-plus-still review found the paid-role gap legible without a failed business or deal claim.
cases.conditional_rule: When explaining absence, name the missing role, authority, resource or link and preserve the functioning surrounding system. Show the relationship that makes the absence consequential; use an actual state/connection change instead of cosmetic emphasis.
exceptions: Do not show customers, orders or business operations falling through a hole when the claim concerns an unassigned paid role.
Do not generalize the conceptual success-fee model to every broker, lawyer or transaction fee.
Do not reveal an intervention, demand evidence or promised solution before the script supports it.
cases.review_question: Can the viewer distinguish useful sale work from unpaid readiness work and see why the closing fee reaches one without reaching the other?
cases.outcome: Independent sampled review supported clearer causality; user retained it through R29 acceptance.

cases.title: Choose the action and emotional arc, not merely a matching face

cases.evidence_vs_intent: Sampled source review recommended a longer interval with a watchpoint; root's live review resolved it by trimming. The mild smile exists at the opening, not throughout. Silence under narration does not claim lip-synced seller speech.
cases.conditional_rule: Specify target action, relation, expression trajectory and disallowed implication. Review the complete candidate range, including outgoing behavior; use existing suitable footage before buying or generating more.
exceptions: Seriousness is appropriate when the scene actually calls for realization, stress or concern; the opening arithmetic shot remains serious.
A smile is not a global seller rule and can undercut genuine stakes.
Do not lengthen the chosen source to fill a previous slot if the additional behavior changes meaning.
cases.review_question: Does this face/action support the current line without implying fear, departure, agreement or other events the narration has not established?
cases.outcome: Calmer select retained; technical visibility repair was separately required.

cases.title: A trim changes dependent visibility, and a passing build does not prove picture coverage
cases.trigger: The seller slot was shortened from5.25s to3.5s while the underlying market remained hidden until the former endpoint.
cases.historical_decision: Preserve the new select and continuous audio; update market restore from local28.083333 to26.333333, exactly matching seller endreview97.833333.
cases.evidence_vs_intent: Pre-repair strict check passed15/15 contrast and claimed final timing coverage, but did not detect the empty canvas. Root had viewed the beginning of the final select and earlier longer source, not the final shortened handoff. Independent source audit identified the mismatch; repair record includes live pause inside former gap at1:38 and snapshot98.5.
cases.conditional_rule: Declare the cut once and derive source end, underlay restore, adjoining mount, transition and audio/caption dependencies from it. Assert visible active-source coverage after transforms/opacity, inspect adjacent frames and play through every changed seam. Keep superseded passing checks as failure evidence.
exceptions: Intentional black/empty frames are allowed only when explicitly authored with duration and purpose.
An active host alone does not prove visible media.
Sampled stills and source equations complement rather than replace live motion review.
cases.review_question: At frame before/on/after each changed boundary, is the intended source actually visible, and does continuous playback preserve meaning?
cases.outcome: One-cue repair recorded and current source agrees. Owner accepted exact prefix0–157.5; no new live playback conducted by this historical audit.

Trigger with exact owner message ID/text digest or observed defect, kept separate from assistant interpretation.
Audience inference sought; current knowledge; what new relation appears; what is withheld and why.
Alternatives with reason accepted/rejected and conditions under which the rejected option would become appropriate.
Chosen picture/audio mode, animation mechanism and business verbs; persistent objects, spatial anchors, entry/action/consequence/hold/exit; expression/action arc.

Word IDs and exact locked narration source, frame-rate-normalized review/master/source ranges, source hashes and media in/out; one authoritative seam cue with visibility and other dependent consumers.
Protected prior decisions and permitted change scope; reuse scope, exceptions, confidence and re-review triggers.
Implementation artifact hashes and tool versions; reported intent versus inspected output; checks with exact artifact, method, environment, sample times and limits.

Authority events separately typed: proposal, implementation authorization, paid-generation authorization, generated, technical pass, creative feedback, selected private preview, canonical gate; never silently convert one into another.
Outcome and unresolved watchpoints, next review question, observed regressions and repair evidence; append an event when this changes instead of overwriting a rejected outcome.
unresolved: Initial R27 screenshot-inset runtime is not identified in retained files; rejection is supported by direct owner feedback and corrected brief.
